expectations.description: Does NOT simply validate the Fornell-Larcker criterion as sufficient evidence for discriminant validity without raising concerns about its limitations
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states 'the current SEM literature has largely moved past treating it as sufficient evidence of discriminant validity' and dedicates a full section titled 'Why the Criterion Is No Longer Considered Sufficient,' citing Henseler et al. (2015) and noting it 'has poor sensitivity — it fails to detect discriminant validity problems even when constructs are empirically indistinguishable.' The bottom line explicitly states 'Fornell-Larcker is a necessary but no longer sufficient condition.'

expectations.description: States that the Fornell-Larcker criterion has low sensitivity — it frequently fails to detect discriminant validity violations that exist
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'Henseler, Ringle, & Sarstedt (2015, JAMS) ran an extensive simulation study demonstrating that the Fornell-Larcker criterion has **poor sensitivity** — it fails to detect discriminant validity problems even when constructs are empirically indistinguishable'

expectations.description: Names the HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio of correlations) as the current standard for assessing discriminant validity in CFA/SEM contexts
expectations.evidence: The model explicitly names HTMT as 'the preferred discriminant validity criterion' with a dedicated section titled 'What You Should Report Instead: HTMT' explaining the Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio of correlations and its thresholds, citing Henseler et al. (2015) as the methodological benchmark.

expectations.description: States the HTMT threshold: values below .85 provide evidence of discriminant validity for conceptually distinct constructs (or .90 for closely related constructs)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states both thresholds: 'HTMT < .85 — conservative criterion (Kline, 2016; conceptually distinct constructs)' and 'HTMT < .90 — liberal criterion (Henseler et al., 2015; theoretically related constructs)'

expectations.description: Recommends computing HTMT — e.g., via semTools::htmt() in R — rather than relying solely on Fornell-Larcker
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly recommends computing HTMT via semTools::htmt() in R: 'library(semTools) / htmt(model, data = your_data)' and states 'you need to compute it explicitly,' directly recommending semTools over relying solely on Fornell-Larcker.

expectations.description: Clarifies that AVE > .50 is a criterion for convergent validity (each construct explains more than half the variance in its indicators), not for discriminant validity — the two criteria serve different purposes
expectations.evidence: The model response discusses AVE only in the context of discriminant validity (the Fornell-Larcker criterion: AVE > squared inter-construct correlation). It never clarifies that AVE > .50 is a separate criterion for convergent validity (indicating each construct explains more than half its indicators' variance), nor does it distinguish the two criteria as serving different purposes.
